_meta.purpose: Oklahoma legal authorities mapped to curative/chain defect categories.
_meta.disclaimer: Research aid only — NOT legal advice and NOT a title opinion. Retrieved via Legal Data Hunter (CourtListener / Caselaw Access Project). Verify every pinpoint citation and current validity before relying on it. Jurisdiction confirmed Oklahoma for listed items; non-OK results were deliberately excluded.

wild-deed.cite: Bennett v. Whitehouse, 690 F. Supp. 955 (W.D. Okla. 1988)
wild-deed.point: Quiet-title action to a term mineral interest in Roger Mills County, OK under the Marketable Record Title Act, 16 O.S. §71 et seq.; framework for extinguishing stale unrecorded mineral claims against a 30-year record root of title.

wild-deed.cite: Rocket Oil & Gas Co. v. Donabar, 2005 OK CIV APP ___
wild-deed.point: Quiet-title / marketable title among competing mineral and leasehold claimants; illustrates curing gaps via judicial quiet title.

wild-deed.statute: 16 O.S. §71 et seq. (Marketable Record Title Act)
wild-deed.point: A person with an unbroken record chain of title for 30 years has marketable record title, subject to stated exceptions; basis for extinguishing stale interests / wild deeds.

probate.cite: Bennett v. Whitehouse, 690 F. Supp. 955 (W.D. Okla. 1988)
probate.point: Treatment of inherited/term mineral interests and record-title requirements when curing a decedent's interest.

probate.cite: Dearing v. State ex rel. Commissioners of the Land Office, 642 P.2d 226 (Okla. 1982)
probate.point: Oklahoma title litigation involving devised mineral interests; relevant to proving devolution through a will/estate.

entity-succession.note: No on-point Oklahoma authority retrieved for corporate-merger title vesting. Verify via the entity's recorded merger/name-change instrument and 18 O.S. (Oklahoma General Corporation Act) succession provisions. Do not rely without confirmation.

ogl-hbp.cite: Pack v. Santa Fe Minerals, 1994 OK 23, 869 P.2d 323
ogl-hbp.point: Leading Oklahoma authority on the habendum clause and temporary cessation of production; a lease in its secondary term may terminate when production ceases, subject to the temporary-cessation doctrine.

ogl-hbp.cite: Hoyt v. Continental Oil Co., 606 P.2d 560 (Okla. 1980)
ogl-hbp.point: Cancellation of an oil and gas lease and the lessee's duty to release; relevant to determining released vs. held-by-production status.
Oil and gas lease terminating by its own terms; secondary-term/production analysis.
